issues: Spelling guidance says 'it does not mean cover again', but 're-cover' (with a hyphen) does mean 'cover again'. This could confuse learners; the distinction should be made clear.
The illustration brief shows rain outside and soup, which suits a cold but does not clearly show getting better. It also does not match the fever example.
The antonym 'get worse' only covers the health sense. No antonym is given for the second meaning (get back something lost), though this is minor.
suggested_fixes: Rewrite the spelling tip: 'Spelling trick: re + cover. Note: recover (get better) is different from re-cover with a hyphen (cover again). Add -y to make the noun recovery.'
Make the illustration show recovery, e.g. a smiling child sitting up in bed, looking brighter, with a parent bringing soup.
Optionally add 'lose' as an antonym for the 'get back' sense, or label the antonym as applying to the health sense.
